_meta.description: Documented irreducible clean-study findings (the conformance floor) per lane. verify.py compares the engine's Issue_Summary against this set: a fired rule NOT listed here is a FAILURE; a listed rule that stops firing is a notable change (not a failure). See KNOWN-RESIDUALS.md for the full rationale.
_meta.rebaselined: 2026-06-29 (corpus mtime 19:32:46; floor moved SDTMIG 11->9 after the DS findings dropped out of the regenerated corpus)
_meta.vacuity_history_2026_07_03_to_2026_08_05: Between 2026-07-03 (family sharding 03b058bf5) and 2026-08-05 both harness scripts invoked the CLI without -f/--family, so only the default CDISC family loaded and none of these CORE/FDA entries could even be read - every run in that window reported PASS while checking nothing. Fixed 2026-08-05 (Fix #153): both scripts resolve every family shipping a package for the lane and pass them as -f, and verify.py now fails a lane outright when a floor rule appears nowhere in the engine report. The recorded PASSes dated 2026-06-29 predate the break and were honest measurements.
_meta.first_honest_rerun_2026_08_05: OVERALL FAIL. All 15 entries then documented still fired (sdtmig 9/9, sendig 6/6 as recorded; Lane R re-measured sdtmig at 8/9 - CORE-000080 had stopped firing) and 31 further clean-study findings appeared that no entry covered: 21 sdtmig (CDISC-CG0359, FDA-SD0037/1078/1082/1149/1240/1321, 14 PMDA-SD*) and 10 sendig (8 CDISC-SEND-*, FDA-SD0062).
_meta.added_2026_08_06: 9 of those 31 were added below on the OWNER'S EXPLICIT RULING (plans/PLAN-sdtm-testdata-gen.md, the two 'RESOLVED 2026-08-05 (owner)' blocks under section R.5), not by fitting the floor to the data: CDISC-CG0359, PMDA-SD2244, PMDA-SD0062 and the five PMDA twins on sdtmig, and FDA-SD0062 on sendig. Lane placement of the SD0062 pair was verified against the shipped packages rather than taken from R.5's 'both': FDA-SD0062 ships in rules-fda-sendig-3-1-1.json and NOT in rules-fda-sdtmig-3-4.json, and PMDA-SD0062 ships in rules-pmda-sdtmig-3-4.json (there is no rules-pmda-sendig-* package at all), so each fires in exactly one lane.
_meta.still_fail_2026_08_06: THE FLOOR IS STILL FAIL, and nothing here should be read as a PASS. 22 of the 31 remain undocumented and unbaselined - 13 on sdtmig (FDA-SD0037/1078/1082/1149/1240/1321, PMDA-SD0037/1078/1082/1152/1240/1321/2287) and 9 on sendig (CDISC-SEND-0112-1/0129-1/0137/0202/0203/0204/0205/0283/0340). FDA-SD1078 / PMDA-SD1078 are explicitly FORBIDDEN from this file by the owner: the rule is right and the generator was wrong, so generate.drop_unpopulated_permissible now emits a Permissible variable only when it is populated. Baselining SD1078 would permanently hide every future 'Permissible variable left empty' regression.
_meta.unmeasured_2026_08_06: The counts above are Lane R's 2026-08-05 measurement at corpus/engine 6440a2836. They have NOT been re-measured since the SD1078 generator fix - that needs a Maven build of the CLI plus a verify.py run, which the lane that made these edits was forbidden to do. Expect the SD1078 fix to also silence floor entries keyed on the mere existence or the label of a now-dropped Permissible column (CORE-000080, FDA-SD1282, PMDA-SD1282 via PPTPTREF; CORE-000594 via ISMSCBCE; GEN-VMCALM-LBL via GFSEQID). Those would show up as 'disappeared' - a notable change, not a failure - and must be re-cited from a real run before any of them is deleted.

CORE-000080.why: NOT FIRING as of the 2026-08-05 re-measurement, and kept rather than deleted. The rule needs --TPTREF present with none of --ELTM/--TPTNUM/--TPT/--STINT/--ENINT; the regenerated pp.json carries PPSTINT and PPENINT, so the --STINT conjunct is false and the rule runs to SUCCESS with no finding. The PP timepoint-companion contradiction it used to document is unchanged and is now carried in full by the FDA-SD1282 entry below. Keeping the id here preserves the citation, keeps verify.py reporting it under 'disappeared' (a notable change, not a failure), and keeps it in the vacuity guard's population - it is still loaded and still executed, which is exactly what that guard checks.

FDA-SD1282.why: PP's IG includes PPTPTREF but not its companions PPTPT/PPTPTNUM/PPELTM, and the rule flags --TPTREF present without them. The companions cannot be added (not in PP's allowed-variable list, so the engine raises GEN-DISALLOW), and PPRFTDTC is Exp so the timing group cannot simply be removed either. This entry carries the PP contradiction previously documented under CORE-000080, which no longer fires.

CORE-000594.why: ISMSCBCE's published library label 'Molecule Secreted by Cells' is flagged not title-case; the rule is stricter than the CDISC library metadata.

CORE-000701.why: Rule requires EPOCH on a dated Findings record, but EPOCH is not in BS's allowed-variable list (adding it raises GEN-DISALLOW-BS).

FDA-SD1077.why: Same BS EPOCH-required-but-forbidden contradiction as CORE-000701, on both BS and GF.

FDA-SD1339.why: The rule requires EPOCH to be populated on any record with a populated --STDTC or --DTC. It fires on SM: SMSTDTC is Expected (so it must be present and populated) while SM's whole IG variable list is STUDYID, DOMAIN, USUBJID, SMSEQ, MIDS, MIDSTYPE, SMSTDTC, SMENDTC, SMSTDY, SMENDY - there is no EPOCH to populate, and adding one raises GEN-DISALLOW. Same shape as the BS EPOCH contradiction, on a different domain. (It no longer fires on BS: the generator leaves EPOCH-less Findings domains dateless, so BS has no populated --DTC to trigger the second conjunct. The earlier 'domain: BS' on this entry described where it used to fire, not what the rule does.)

FDA-SD0021.why: Start time-point rule requires MHSTDTC, but populating it then requires MHSTDY which the IG omits and the model forbids adding (FDA-SD1087/CORE-000328). Also fires on DS for the same start-time-point reason.

FDA-SD0022.why: End time-point counterpart of FDA-SD0021; same MH start/end-vs-study-day contradiction.

GEN-VMCALM-LBL.why: GFSEQID's library label is literally 'Sequence Identifier \n' (a stray escape, a library-metadata defect). The cleaned label is flagged by the library-match rule; emitting the raw label trips the title-case rule instead.

CDISC-CG0359.why: DM.ARMNRS's published CDISC Library label is 'Reason Arm and/or Actual Arm is Null'. The title-case regex exempts only a fixed list of articles, prepositions and conjunctions; 'and/or' IS in that list but 'is' is a verb and SDTMIG 2.6 item 3h does not exempt verbs, so no conformant label exists for the published one. The rule is CORRECT and the library label is the defect (the conforming form would be '... Actual Arm Is Null'). Escalate upstream to CDISC; do not weaken the regex.

PMDA-SD2244.why: FDA-SD2244 requires TSVCDREF == 'ISO 3166' for TSPARMCD == 'FCNTRY'; PMDA-SD2244 requires 'GENC' or 'ISO 3166-1 alpha-3'. The emitted row ('FCNTRY', 'USA', 'ISO 3166') satisfies FDA and violates PMDA, and 'ISO 3166-1 alpha-3' would simply invert the pair. No single value satisfies both shipped rules - a genuine FDA-vs-PMDA authority conflict, not a data defect.

PMDA-SD0062.why: extract_metadata('file_format') is neither SAS transport (XPORT) nor text-delimited: the lane ships Dataset-JSON by settled plan decision 4. A harness artifact of a decision the plan already records; the alternative is emitting a parallel .xpt lane. Ships only in the pmda sdtmig packages (there is no rules-pmda-sendig-* package), so this id is an sdtmig-lane residual only - its sendig counterpart is FDA-SD0062.

PMDA-SD0021.why: Family twin of FDA-SD0021 - Check and Scope byte-identical; same irreducible MH start-time-point-vs-study-day contradiction reported a second time by a second family.

PMDA-SD0022.why: Family twin of FDA-SD0022 - Check and Scope byte-identical; same irreducible contradiction reported by a second family.

PMDA-SD1077.why: Family twin of FDA-SD1077 - Check and Scope byte-identical; same irreducible EPOCH-required-but-not-in-the-allowed-variable-list contradiction reported by a second family.

PMDA-SD1282.why: Family twin of FDA-SD1282 - Check identical (Scope differs in shape, Classes + Domains.Exclude vs Domains ALL, but resolves to the same PP finding); same irreducible PP timepoint-companion contradiction reported by a second family.

PMDA-SD1339.why: Family twin of FDA-SD1339 - Check identical, Scope narrower (PMDA additionally excludes DX, DO, DU, SC, DS, DT, MH); same irreducible SM EPOCH contradiction reported by a second family.

CORE-000328.why: SEND SE has SESTDTC/SEENDTC (Req) but no SESTDY/SEENDY columns in the model; the study-day rule requires them and the engine forbids adding them (GEN-DISALLOW).

CORE-000776.why: Same SE study-day-column contradiction as CORE-000328.

FDA-SD1087.why: Same SE study-day-column contradiction as CORE-000328.

FDA-SD1091.why: Same SE study-day-column contradiction as CORE-000328.

FDA-SD0029.why: TF has Req TFRESCAT forcing a populated --STRESC, but TF has no --STRESU column, so a populated --STRESC necessarily trips FDA-SD0029 (itself 'Partially Executable - Possible Overreporting'). This is the minimal residual (1 finding vs 3).

FDA-SE2307.why: BG/FW are interval findings with --DTC + --ENDTC but no --STDTC. FDA-SE2307 wants --DY and --ENDY both populated; populating --ENDTC trips CORE-000892 and populating --ENDY without a complete --ENDTC trips FDA-SD1093, so leaving --ENDY empty (FDA-SE2307) is the floor.

FDA-SD0062.why: extract_metadata('file_format') is neither SAS transport (XPORT) nor text-delimited: the lane ships Dataset-JSON by settled plan decision 4. Identical mechanism to the sdtmig lane's PMDA-SD0062. Ships only in the fda sendig packages - it is absent from rules-fda-sdtmig-3-4.json - so this id is a sendig-lane residual only.
